meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: derived from ramp_far_end=motorway: every exit-ramp chain merges onto another motorway, so nothing stops traffic at the far end. Free flow is inferred from read OSM link topology, not from a tag -- OSM does not tag the absence of a control. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-08-19: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: derived from ramp_far_end=motorway: every exit-ramp chain merges onto another motorway, so nothing stops traffic at the far end. Free flow is inferred from read OSM link topology, not from a tag -- OSM does not tag the absence of a control. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-08-19: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop node on a motorway_link way within 1400 m of this exit's junctions, read from the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16; no control stood at a walked terminal: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: derived from ramp_far_end=motorway: every exit-ramp chain merges onto another motorway, so nothing stops traffic at the far end. interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

crossings.name: Mackinac Bridge

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
